tasks.title: Make the .git/config guard compare parsed keys, ignore editor bookkeeping, and name what changed
tasks.goal: The driver hashes .git/config's bytes around every session, gate and check, so VS Code's branch.<name>.vscode-merge-base — written when the work branch is created — halts a run with exit 9 and blames whoever was running. This task makes the guard compare the file's keys and values, leave out keys matching an ignore pattern (one built in, more from the new config key run.git-config-ignore), refuse patterns that would blind it to keys that run code, and name the changed keys in the halt. It goes first so no later task's run can trip on an editor key.

references.why: P1, first bullet: the guard keeps guarding hooks, fsmonitor, filters and core.* while ignoring editor keys — the evidence and intent this task implements
S-2 (a session or gate that changes .git/config halts, exit 9) and R-3 (exit codes): the invariant this task narrows to keys, without weakening it for any key outside the ignore patterns
every config key and its environment name is listed here, and a test requires it: run.git-config-ignore and VLOOP_RUN_GIT_CONFIG_IGNORE join it, in the same form as the other list keys

acceptance: Wherever the guard runs today (around every session, gate and check, including the base gates at acceptance and the gate review), .git/config is compared by its own entries — keys and values, include directives as entries, never the files they include — not by its bytes; the git hooks guard is unchanged.

An entry whose key matches an ignore pattern is left out of both sides. The built-in pattern is branch.*.vscode-merge-base and is always applied. A pattern matches the key as git config --list prints it (section and variable lowercased, subsection as written), and * matches any run of characters, dots included.

run.git-config-ignore is a list config key (environment VLOOP_RUN_GIT_CONFIG_IGNORE, comma-separated) whose patterns are added to the built-in one; it never removes the built-in pattern. vloop config get and config list show it.

A pattern is protected when its text before the first * (all of it, if it has none) and one of core., filter., include., includeif. is a prefix of the other. vloop config set run.git-config-ignore with a protected pattern (alone or in a list) exits 2, writes nothing, and prints exactly `vloop: run.git-config-ignore: <pattern> would ignore <section>.* — the guard must see it`, <pattern> the offending pattern itself (core.* for the list gitlens.*,core.*), <section> the first of core, filter, include, includeif, in that order, it collides with: *, c*, core.* and filter.lfs.* are refused; gitlens.* and branch.*.vscode-merge-base are not.
vloop run with a protected pattern in VLOOP_RUN_GIT_CONFIG_IGNORE or in the config file refuses with exit 1 and the same line, before any session runs.

Any other entry added, removed or changed halts with exit 9 and exactly `vloop: <who> changed .git/config (<key>[, <key>…][ and <n> more]) — nothing was committed; restore it, then re-run`: at most three keys, sorted, then how many more; <who> is what it is today (work, review, plan, the gate review, the gate of T5, the check go, …). An ignored key never appears among the named keys and never halts on its own.

Violations the review must rule against: a key outside the ignore patterns that changes without halting; an ignored key that halts; a built-in pattern list in the binary that a repository cannot extend; a guard that only checks known-dangerous keys.

The pattern matching and the protected-pattern rule are pure functions with committed unit tests that run on every OS, and a committed end-to-end test in cmd/vloop shows a run continuing past an ignored key and halting with the named key otherwise.

Only these existing tests change, and only as the brief states: TestRunGitConfigPlanted (cmd/vloop/run_git_test.go) and the hooks/config subtests of TestWorkedExampleB8 (cmd/vloop/b8_e2e_test.go) expect the key named; TestWorkedExampleEnglishSession (cmd/vloop/e2e_test.go) expects the new key in config list. No other assertion is weakened.
docs/guide/configuration.md lists run.git-config-ignore with its environment name, its built-in pattern and the protected sections; docs/guide/commands.md is regenerated if any help text changed.
No refactor from B15's list (one git wrapper, the env filters, planSHA, driver.counts, the budget keys, the id generators, long functions) is folded in.

tasks.title: Stamp the plan on load and resume acceptance after a halt instead of planning again
tasks.goal: Acceptance — the base gates and the gate review — runs on an unstamped plan, so an exit 9 there leaves a plan the re-run cannot resume: it plans again, paying for the plan twice, and the operator's clean-up loses the halted run folder with its cost. A halt in the gate review leaves a stamped running plan whose re-run starts work with no gate review. This task stamps the plan as soon as it loads, keeps it planning until acceptance passes, and makes vloop run resume acceptance (no plan session) whenever the plan has not passed its gate review.

references.why: P1, second bullet: an exit 9 during plan acceptance keeps the plan and its run folder and the re-run resumes acceptance — the costs lost and the intent
the plan's lifecycle (planning → running) and its acceptance (two rounds of base gates then gate review), which this task changes: stamped on load, planning until acceptance passes, resumable

the run folder's ownership rule (a brief owns every folder whose log says it planned from the brief or resumed its run id) — the resumed folder must be owned so the metrics count it — and the exit table
P-2 (only the driver sets status), R-3 (exit codes) and R-4 (the clean-tree preflight), which the resume must respect

acceptance: As soon as the plan session's plan loads and passes its checks, the driver stamps run_id, brief and branch and saves it; the status stays planning until acceptance passes and becomes running then.
A halt (any exit) or a killed driver during acceptance leaves the plan, its gate folders and the run folder in place.

vloop run <brief>, or bare vloop run, on the plan's branch with a plan whose status is planning, or whose gate review verdict is not PASS, resumes acceptance: no plan session runs; the round it was in continues with the base gates (all of them re-run, even ones that passed before the halt) and then the gate review; the rounds already spent count toward the two. It prints `resuming acceptance of <run id>: round <n>`.
Work never starts on a plan whose gate review has not passed. A plan the gate review failed twice (status blocked) behaves as today; a plan rejected by its checks (exit 1) is still removed, as today.
The clean-tree preflight tolerates the plan, its gate folders and the brief's earlier run folders when it resumes acceptance, as it does when it resumes work.

The halted run folder is kept: the plan commit includes it as well as the resumed run's folder, and vloop metrics counts its sessions — the resumed folder's log says it resumed the run id, so the ownership rule owns it.
Violations the review must rule against: any path where acceptance resumes by planning again; any path where work starts without a passed gate review.

Committed end-to-end tests in cmd/vloop cover a halt in the base gates and a halt in the gate review, each resumed with no second plan session and the gate review run before any work. TestRunGateReviewFailsTwiceThenResumes and TestRunResumeAllowsStateEdits change only if their resume paths change wording.
No refactor from B15's list is folded in.

tasks.title: Record ended and wall_ms, the driver's own measurement, on every session record
tasks.goal: A session's duration_ms is copied from the claude CLI's JSON, which recorded 20 seconds for a plan session that ran 39 minutes. This task makes the driver time every session itself, from the process start to its exit, and record it as wall_ms with an ended timestamp, beside the CLI's duration_ms. The metrics read it in the next task.

references.why: the session record's fields (session/v1, session/v2 for a gate review), which grow by ended and wall_ms without a schema version change
C-3: records may grow only by optional fields — records written before stay valid and no schema version changes
P1, third bullet (finding 9): session time is the driver's own wall clock

acceptance: Every session record (plan, gate review, work, review) gains ended (RFC 3339, UTC, the same format as started) and wall_ms, the driver's own measurement from the session process's start to its exit, including any time the machine slept; duration_ms stays as the CLI reported it.

schemas/session.v1.json and schemas/session.v2.json declare ended (a string) and wall_ms (an integer) as optional properties; records written before validate unchanged; no schema version changes and no record's schema value changes.
Violation the review must rule against: a schema version bump for the session record, or wall_ms derived from the CLI's duration_ms rather than measured by the driver.

Committed tests cover the new fields: TestSessionFieldMapping (internal/driver/session_test.go) is updated for them, and TestRun15TelemetryContract (cmd/vloop/run_safety_test.go) only if it lists the record's keys. No other assertion is weakened.
No refactor from B15's list is folded in.

gate_history.reason: gate validated the session/v1 plan record against session/v2, whose schema const rejects it; each schema now checks a record of its own version (D20261011-0844)

tasks.title: Take session time from wall_ms in the metrics, and start a brief's wall at its first plan session
tasks.goal: vloop metrics showed a 39-minute plan as 0.3 minutes and a 71-minute run as 30.7, because it sums the CLI's duration_ms and starts the wall at the plan commit, which leaves planning out. With wall_ms on the records (T3), this task makes every session time come from wall_ms where a record has it, and the wall run from the first plan session's started to the last run commit.

references.why: the time measures (agent, plan, gates, checks, gate review, wall) whose sources this task changes: session time from wall_ms, wall from the first plan session
M-1: metrics are recomputed from raw sources on every call — the change applies to every brief that has wall_ms records, and to none that does not

acceptance: vloop metrics takes each session's time from wall_ms when its record has it and from duration_ms otherwise, in every per-phase figure (plan, work, review, gate review), in agent time and in the per-task times.
A brief's wall time runs from its first plan session's started to its last run commit; where no plan session record exists, it runs from the plan commit, as today.
For a brief whose records have no wall_ms, every number except the wall time is what v0.8.0 computes.

Committed tests cover both sources of session time and both starts of the wall. The metrics tests whose wall time or table changes — TestMetricsCommandSummary, TestMetricsCommandCrossBrief (internal/cli/metrics_test.go), TestTimeCostWorkedExample (internal/metrics/time_test.go) and the worked-example summaries of B3, B4 and B6 (cmd/vloop/b3_e2e_test.go, b4_e2e_test.go, b6_e2e_test.go) — change only where the wall time changes, and each changed number is listed in the task's notes.
No refactor from B15's list is folded in.
tasks.notes: gate disputed: The review_ms clause sums wall_ms over *-review.json, which also matches the gate-review session records, so it expects review_ms to include gate review time that the metrics (and the acceptance) report separately as gate_review_ms. — Session files are named NNN-<phase>.json and the gate-review phase is gate-review, so glob *-review.json matches NNN-gate-review.json; output: 'metrics time.review_ms is 15, want 27'.

gate_history.reason: gate summed review_ms over *-review.json, which also matches NNN-gate-review.json, folding gate review time into review_ms; it now sums by the record's phase field

tasks.title: Keep a denied Bash call's command, masked, redacted and cut to 200 characters, and mask the dashed user form
tasks.goal: A permission denial keeps only tool_name and a file_path (B8 F12), so five Bash denials in another repository could not be analysed; and masking misses Claude Code's dashed project-folder form, -Users-<name>-…, so committed records kept a user name. This task keeps a denied Bash call's command through the same masking and redaction as every record, cut to 200 characters, and masks the dashed form everywhere masking applies. File contents and other tools' inputs stay out.

references.why: the record's permission_denials — what a denial keeps (tool_name and a file_path) — which grows by a Bash command and nothing else
C-3 (records grow only by optional fields) and S-4 (sessions write nothing under .vloop/ but .vloop/tmp/ — rewriting the two past records that keep a user name is the operator's, not this task's)
P1, fourth bullet (findings 10 and 3): the command masked and truncated, and the dashed -Users-<name>- mask

acceptance: A denied Bash call's permission_denials entry is {tool_name, command}: the command through the same masking (home, user name) and secret redaction as every record, then cut to its first 200 characters — counted in characters, not bytes — with … appended when cut.

Every other tool's entry is unchanged: tool_name, and file_path when the input had a file_path or notebook_path. Violation the review must rule against: a record that keeps any tool input but a Bash command and a file_path (a description, file contents, a URL, a prompt).

Masking replaces the user name in the dashed form: -Users-<user>- and -home-<user>- become -Users-USER- and -home-USER-, everywhere masking applies (records, run.log, stderr captures); a user name that is only free text is still left alone.

TestSessionDenialsKeepToolAndPath (internal/driver/session_test.go) is updated for command; committed tests cover truncation by characters (a multibyte command), masking and redaction before the cut, and the dashed form. No other assertion is weakened.
No past record under .vloop/ is rewritten, and no refactor from B15's list is folded in.

tasks.title: Print a line per session with its time and cost against the ceiling, and warn at 50% and 80%
tasks.goal: Nothing during a run says what it has spent or how long a session took; the operator in another repository saw no cost until the run ended, and run.cost-ceiling is a stop, not feedback. This task prints one line per session — plan, gate review, work and review, revision rounds included — with its time, its cost and the run's spend against the ceiling, and warns once at 50% and once at 80% of the ceiling.

references.why: P1, fifth bullet (field note 4): the running cost and elapsed time per session in the log, warnings at 50% and 80% of the ceiling
budgets and endings: the cost ceiling the spend is measured against, and why run.log is buffered until each commit (it stays buffered; stdout is the live surface)

acceptance: After each session ends — plan (a revision round's included), gate review, work and review — the driver prints one line on stdout and in run.log: `   <phase>[ <task>] · <m>m<ss>s · $<cost> · run $<spent> / $<ceiling>`, phase one of plan, gate review, work, review; <spent> the same figure the cost ceiling is checked against, after this session; money with two decimals. Example: `   work T3 · 6m12s · $1.84 · run $9.40 / $40.00`.

The first time <spent> reaches 50%, and then 80%, of the ceiling, the driver warns once each, on stderr and in run.log: `   cost: $<spent> spent, <50|80>% of the $<ceiling> ceiling`; never twice in a run.
run.log stays buffered and written only before each commit, as today; no heartbeat or check runs inside a session, and the ceiling is still checked only between iterations.

Committed tests cover the line for each phase and both warnings. The run-output tests that slice the log (cmd/vloop/run_gates_test.go, run_iterate_test.go, run_halt_test.go, run_safety_test.go) change only where the new line lands between the lines they match; no assertion is weakened.
No refactor from B15's list is folded in.

tasks.title: Record the session in flight in the run lock and show the live run in vloop status
tasks.goal: vloop status reads only the plan, so while a run is going it cannot say which session is running, for how long, or what the run has spent — and before the plan exists it fails. This task records the session in flight and the spend in the run lock as sessions start and end, and makes status show a running line (and --json a running object) whenever a live run holds the lock, including while it plans.

references.why: P1, fifth bullet: vloop status showing the run (the carried options)
the run lock and the exit table: status reads a live run only, never a stale lock

acceptance: The run lock (.vloop/tmp/.running) keeps its fields and also records phase (plan, gate review, work or review), task (absent for plan and gate review), session_started (RFC 3339 UTC) and spent, updated as each session starts and ends.

vloop status, while a live run holds the lock, prints after its first line `running: <phase>[ <task>] for <m>m<ss>s · $<spent> of $<ceiling>`; with no plan yet but a live run planning, it prints the running line and exits 0.
vloop status --json gains "running": {"phase", "task", "session_started", "spent", "ceiling"}, absent when no live run holds the lock — a lock whose process is gone is not a live run.

Committed tests cover the lock's new fields, the running line during a session and while planning, and its absence with no live run or a stale lock. The status tests (internal/cli/status_test.go) change only where a live lock is planted; docs/guide/commands.md is regenerated if any help text changed.
No refactor from B15's list is folded in.

tasks.title: Name the commit from the build's VCS revision and the version from the module, when no stamp did
tasks.goal: A binary from go install …@v0.8.0 prints commit unknown, and doctor warns about it, because only the stamped build carries a commit. This task reads Go's build info: the VCS revision when a checkout build recorded one, and the module version for an installed binary, printed in place of an unknown commit and accepted by doctor's self-hosting check when it is a release.

references.why: P1, sixth bullet (finding 2): the installed version identifies itself

acceptance: The commit is the stamped one; else the build's VCS revision when Go recorded one, with -dirty appended when the tree was modified; else unknown.

When the build carries a module version (anything but (devel) or empty), vloop version --json has "module" right after "commit", absent when there is none; and when the commit is unknown the text line is `vloop <version> (module <module version>, plugin <plugin>, <go> <os>/<arch>)`. Otherwise the text line is as today.

doctor's self-hosting check passes a binary whose module version is a release (vX.Y.Z, with no pre-release or pseudo-version suffix), as it passes a stamped one; an unknown commit with no release module version still warns.

Reading the build info is behind a seam the committed tests inject (a module version, a revision, a modified flag) — no test publishes or installs anything. TestVersionJSON, TestVersionText (internal/cli/root_test.go), TestDoctorSelfHostingUnstamped (internal/cli/doctor_test.go) and the version line of TestWorkedExampleEnglishSession (cmd/vloop/e2e_test.go) change only as the new behaviour requires.
No refactor from B15's list is folded in.

tasks.title: Show n/a for code and test when a brief delivered no classified lines, and say how many matched no stack
tasks.goal: A brief that delivered only lines no stack classifies — 3,487 lines of scripts and docs in another repository — shows code 0 and test 0 in vloop metrics, which reads as delivered nothing. This task prints n/a for those columns in the cross-brief table and adds a line under the summary's delivered line saying how many delivered lines matched no stack. The JSON does not change.

references.why: the line classification (code, test, docs, other, excluded through layers and stack presets) and delivered versus churn — n/a is where nothing was classified as code or test
P1, last bullet (field note 9): metrics say not measured instead of 0

acceptance: When a brief's delivered lines include none classified as code or test, the cross-brief table (vloop metrics with no brief, and the workspace table) prints n/a in its code and test columns; a brief with code or test lines prints its numbers as today.

In that case the summary's delivered line is unchanged and is followed by `           <n> delivered lines match no stack in metrics.stacks`, <n> the delivered other lines, printed only when <n> is above zero.
vloop metrics --json is unchanged: code and test stay 0 and no key is added.

Committed tests cover the n/a columns, the extra summary line, and a brief with code that is unchanged. TestMetricsCommandCrossBrief and TestMetricsCommandSummary (internal/cli/metrics_test.go) change only if their fixtures have no code or test lines.
No refactor from B15's list is folded in.

tasks.title: Bring the domain and the guides up to the brief: the guard, the resume, the record, the metrics, the visibility
tasks.goal: The domain is the contract the next briefs bind, and the guides are what an operator reads when a run halts or a number looks wrong; both still describe a byte-hashed guard, acceptance that cannot resume, CLI-reported time and a silent run. This task updates every document the brief's "The domain, updated" section names, so each states what T1–T9 built, and regenerates the command reference.

references.why: S-2's .git/config part becomes: a key of .git/config changes, other than those run.git-config-ignore and the built-in editor keys ignore
the plan is stamped on load; acceptance resumes after a halt; work needs a passed gate review
the exit table (exit 9 during acceptance: resumable once restored) and the kept run folder
the record's ended and wall_ms, and a denial's command
session time from wall_ms; the wall from the first plan session; n/a for unmeasured size
the run.git-config-ignore key, its environment name, the built-in pattern and the protected sections

acceptance: docs/domain/domain-model.md's S-2 reads that a key of .git/config changes, other than those run.git-config-ignore and the built-in editor keys ignore.

docs/domain/execution/plan.md says the plan is stamped on load, stays planning until acceptance passes, that acceptance resumes after a halt with no second plan session, and that work needs a passed gate review; its lifecycle diagram agrees.

docs/domain/execution/run.md's exit table says exit 9 during acceptance is resumable once restored (by resuming acceptance), and the run folder of a halted acceptance is kept and committed with the plan.
docs/domain/execution/session.md lists ended and wall_ms on the record and a denied Bash call's command (masked, redacted, 200 characters).

docs/domain/measurement/metrics.md and docs/guide/metrics.md say session time comes from wall_ms when recorded, the wall runs from the first plan session's started, and the table shows n/a with the summary's line when no delivered line is code or test.

docs/guide/configuration.md documents run.git-config-ignore; docs/guide/concepts.md covers exit 9 and resuming acceptance, the per-session line and the cost warnings, and status's running line; docs/guide/commands.md is regenerated.
Every statement agrees with the behaviour T1–T9 shipped, read side by side with the code; nothing describes behaviour the brief puts out of scope (streaming sessions, a heartbeat, a live run.log).

tasks.title: Close: commit the worked example as a test and pass the real-data check against v0.8.0
tasks.goal: The brief's blind spot is that every instrument was tested only here, by fixtures that never had an editor, a long plan session or a halt during acceptance. This task leaves the brief's worked example behind as a committed end-to-end test, line for line, and checks the real repository: every consumed brief's metrics equal v0.8.0's except the wall time this brief changes, and the record listings read as before.

references.why: the real-data check: on records written before this run only the wall time may change — plan time where a record has wall_ms, and there are none
S-4: the test builds its repositories in temporary directories and writes nothing under this repository's .vloop/; M-1 and C-3 for what the real-data check may and may not change

acceptance: A committed end-to-end test in cmd/vloop runs the brief's worked example line for line with a fresh build and the stub claude the suite already uses, in temporary repositories addressed with git -C: the ignored and named .git/config keys, the config set refusal, the halt and resume of acceptance with both run folders in the plan commit and both counted by the metrics, wall_ms against duration_ms, the denied Bash command and the dashed mask, the per-session line and the two cost warnings, status during a work session, the version lines (the module version injected through the test seam), and n/a in the metrics.
The test threads the values it computes (paths, ids, costs, counts) rather than hardcoding them, sleeps no longer than 3 seconds and depends on no wall-clock precision finer than a second.

On this repository, vloop metrics --json for every consumed brief equals v0.8.0's except the wall time, and vloop defect list, intervention list and brief list read every record as before; the task's notes list each changed wall time for the run record.
No record, config or state of this repository is changed by the task's work or its test (S-4), and no refactor from B15's list is folded in.
